outcome: Report arithmetic and comparisons that combine columns whose declared units differ (issue 17, item 2): a unit declared on a column follows it through the transform language, an addition, subtraction or comparison of two operands with different declared units is named in unit_mismatch advice on the successful response, and derived and aggregated columns carry the unit their inputs agree on, without refusing, converting or changing any value
criteria: With the issue's reproduction (probe_measurements with sales declared USD and return_rate declared percent, a derive of sales + return_rate), transform_dataset still succeeds with mixed_measure = 105.0, its advice has kind unit_mismatch naming both columns, both units and the derive step, and mixed_measure carries no unit

Units that are the same after case folding and whitespace collapsing (USD and usd) produce no advice and give the derived column that unit, shown in the preview's result columns and in the materialized dataset's schema; an operand whose unit is not declared produces no advice and leaves the result's unit unknown; multiplication, division and modulo never warn and give no unit; units of different scale or currency (yuan and ten-thousand yuan, USD and EUR) are reported and nothing is converted; a comparison of two such columns in a filter is reported the same way

The propagation rules are documented and hold: a column keeps its unit through select, filter, sort, limit, rename and semi_join, a join brings each right column's own unit, sum, avg, min and max keep their field's unit and count gives none, abs, round, floor, ceil, negation and numeric casts keep their operand's unit, raw_query output columns have none, and a materialized dataset stores the units of its columns so a later transform over it is checked too; a new MADR records the rule, and README.md, the transform_dataset tool description and the recovery module docstring describe it

Nothing else changes: no transform is refused for its units, result values and types are the same as before, and tests under tests/ with fixtures unrelated to DataSpace cover each case above; the backend test suite passes

reason: Bind the decision record this work wrote for the unit rule, MADR 0019, as criterion 3 names it

note: agent_backend/core/ir/units.py walks the canonical steps with a name-to-unit map seeded from the declared units of the source columns (by column id) and records a UnitConflict for +, - and comparisons in a derive or filter. The backend builds the report once per transform; advise_units turns conflicts into one unit_mismatch advice, preview result columns list known units, and _commit_materialization stores the inferred unit on every materialized column. MADR 0019 was written in this outcome and bound by amendment. tests/test_units.py has 13 tests; the backend suite passes (447). The 8 media tests still fail because the local FFmpeg lacks a video encoder, unrelated to this change.
